$comment: Authoring input for `npm run sprites:emotions`. Nothing here ships to the browser — it
is the prompt book for the Ludo.ai generator, and the record of what each clip was asked
to be, so a re-run reproduces the same intent.
Prompt rules learned the hard way, keep to them:
- Describe POSTURE, not expression. A Trial sprite's face is 50-80px on screen; a raised
eyebrow is invisible and asking for one just wastes the model's attention.
- Say 'in place', 'no travel'. Left unsaid, the model walks the animal out of frame and
the clip cannot loop against a static stage slot.
- Framing comes from each animal's `view`, never from the prompt text: the cast is NOT
uniformly side-on. The owl is drawn front-facing and the raccoon's sitting pose is a
three-quarter — telling either of them 'side view, facing left' asks the generator to
turn the character, and the clip then will not cut against its own idle loop.
- Keep the silhouette. The reference frame carries the character; the prompt should only
ever move it.
- Never name a posture the animal has to CHANGE STATE to reach. 'Crouched low' made the
generator lie the donkey down over the clip and never stand it back up: a transition,
not a held attitude, and one that cannot loop. Say what the body does while it stays
where it is, and say outright what it must not do ('never lies down').
- Watch the height swing in the review output. The runtime scales a clip off one union
bounding box, so a character whose height wanders 20%+ across frames renders too small
for most of the clip however good it looks in isolation.

white-sheep-1.$comment: The sheep's carrier is CONTRAST, not shape: a solid black head and black floppy ears against a pale fleece, which is the strongest value contrast in the cast — head height, head tilt and ear position read at any size, while the fleece is a fluffy oval that deforms into mush if you ask it to do anything. Its own hazard is a GRAZING prior (the atlas even ships `eating`): a sheep prompt will drop the head to the ground and stay there, which is a pose collapse that cannot loop. Suppressed the way the owl's wings finally were — by asserting positively that the head stays up at the reference height, not by forbidding grazing. Note the source canvas is only 419x363, the smallest in the cast, so generated detail is softer here than for the fox.

raccoon.$comment: Staged sitting up on the trial stand (`idleTrial`), so the reference is the sitting pose, not the four-legged crouch — a clip generated from the crouch would pop the moment the debate cuts to it. Its carrier is the FACE: big white eyes inside a dark bandit mask with heavy dark brows above them, the highest-contrast face in the cast after the owl, so brows and eyes do the emotional work. It is also the only character with FREE FOREPAWS — it can gesture, point and clench, which no other animal here can. Both of its priors come from those same paws: they rest in exactly the 'holding something' pose and the atlas ships `eat_nut` and `throw_nut`, so a nut will appear unless the paws are positively described as empty; and a sitting animal is one prompt away from dropping back onto all fours. Both suppressed per rule 6 by naming what holds.

owl.$comment: A standing bird has no gait and no shoulders to square, so the generic four-legged posture prompts read as nonsense here. Two hazards this body has and the quadrupeds do not — it can TAKE OFF, and the word 'perch' invites a branch the source art does not contain — so every prompt forbids both. Its angry clip took five attempts: forbidding the wing flare never worked (an 'angry bird' prior outweighs any 'never spread' instruction) and only freezing the body positively did — 'body, wings and feet stay exactly as in the reference, ONLY THE FACE MOVES'. AND THE BIG ONE: this owl breaks the global 'posture, not expression' rule. Its eyes are ~40% of its body area in high-contrast yellow, so the face IS the silhouette and reads fine at stage scale. The first pass proved it — a body-posture 'angry' read as a surprised owl talking, while 'sneaky' asking for narrowed eyes was the best clip generated for any animal. Lead the owl's emotions with eyes, brow and beak.

It never takes off and never leaves the ground; no perch or branch appears. Seamless loop, no travel, same silhouette throughout.

ONLY THE FACE MOVES. The brow feathers press down into a hard V over the eyes, each big yellow eye narrows into a slanted slit with the bright yellow still visible, and the beak opens and snaps shut in a sharp scolding. The head tips forward a little toward the viewer and back. Nothing else in the picture changes. Starts and ends in the exact pose of the reference image. Seamless loop, no travel, same silhouette throughout.
